+# Iteration 0.011 · n = 5 of 99 · 2026-09-24 · author: twelve lenses · round 5
+
+## Twelve lenses
+
+### Aset
+SSSES (business case): security 84 · stability 70 · scalability 68 · efficiency 67 · succinctness 64
+
+Founder, investors, customers: the register holds after round four, and I checked every echo I named. The ladder still reads in one order on S1, S2, S11, S15, S16 and S17; the declared model is stated in the same words on S3, S8 and S15; the citizen's answer now appears on S4, S7, S12, S13, S17 and S18 without contradiction. This round the theme gains a body: one event worked in minutes on S4, reconciling to the ninety minutes and the rate S3 already declares. That is reinforcement, not repetition, because each appearance adds a fact. The two horizon echoes on S14 and S17 stay, since each carries a different column.

+### Asar
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 70 · scalability 69 · efficiency 67 · succinctness 63
+
+Read whole, the deck now answers the question a system thinker asked in round four: show me one event with numbers. S4's note walks an EDU event twice, benchmark alone and the one platform, minute by minute, and the difference is the ninety minutes S3 prices. The synthesis for the founder: the value equation is no longer an abstraction, it is a clock a president can recognise. For investors: the build calendar on S14 ties every year of spend to what ships that year. For customers: the same instrument rehearses a public body's policy posture before adoption. Nothing is claimed; every figure is an assumption until the tabletop stamps real clocks.

+words: 111

+### Athena
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 72 · scalability 69 · efficiency 70 · succinctness 64
+
+Strategy is sequence, calendar, and now a build plan beneath the calendar. Round four dated the gates; this round dates the work. The eleven-year spend already existed as a number per year; S14 now says what each year buys: measurement design in 2026, the seven objects and the trial in 2027, absorption by qualification through 2030, the platform tier and sustain after. Investors can hold the spend against the deliverable. Execution leaders can see the critical path: the G2 tabletop precedes the seven objects, the trial precedes the first six accounts. Founder, the strategic risk unchanged is the named institution; no calendar substitutes for one. Ask the EDU president this quarter.
+
+words: 111

+### Christo
+SSSES (business case): security 81 · stability 70 · scalability 69 · efficiency 66 · succinctness 65
+
+The people a decision touches are on the page, and this round they gain a rehearsal. S16 said the same scenario runs twice, benchmark alone against the one platform. Now the note says a public body can run a policy posture the same way before adopting it, and the citizens who answered can replay what was decided and why. That is consensus as a practice, not a slogan: ask, decide with named authority, show the result, learn together. Founder, this is how the platform earns trust across a community rather than inside a cabinet. Investors, trust that is rehearsed is retained. Customers, you are participants in the record, never only recipients.

+words: 111

+### Enki
+SSSES (business case): security 80 · stability 69 · scalability 67 · efficiency 65 · succinctness 63
+
+Edge cases keep the case honest, so I tested the worked event. The example assumes a cabinet that convenes in twenty minutes and a president reachable on a Tuesday. The edge is the event at three in the morning with the approver unreachable; succession of decision rights on S14 covers it, and the example says so by labelling itself an assumption until the tabletop stamps real clocks. The second edge: the build calendar assumes the seven objects ship in the first half of 2027 while the trial runs. If the trial changes an object, the calendar moves. The record carries that; the input changes, the deck re-derives, the register says why.

A builder can open that note and start a schema; no research problem is in it. S14 carries the build calendar against the spend: 2026 buys the measurement design, 2027 buys the objects and the trial, 2028 to 2030 buys absorption one function at a time. +### Krishna
+SSSES (business case): security 83 · stability 71 · scalability 71 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 64
+
+Integration is where one-platform claims break, so I traced the new lines. The worked event on S4 names the feeds as they enter: the alert from the campus system, facts on the record, objectives, posture, release with a named owner, acknowledgement. Every hop is a pointer or an approval, never a copy of another system's data. The data-model note on S6 says which object each write lands in, which is the contract an integration partner reads first. S16 extends the instrument to a public body without adding a component: the polling interface is the inbound and the outbound. Investors see one architecture; customers see one login and one record, both unchanged.

+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 70 · scalability 72 · efficiency 67 · succinctness 65

That is the foresight this round buys: examples derived from inputs outlive the tools that produced them. For the founder, the next three years decide whether the decision record or the incumbent's bundled module owns the executive door; the calendar on S14 is your answer.
